title: Hosted API token econ decision-tree proposals
summary: Working worksheet that converts the hosted API unit-econ spreadsheet into a decision tree for routing calls by latency slice, region, and model family. Goal: produce a small set of deterministic routing rules that map request attributes to an expected per-token COGS band and an operational fallback. This is a hypothesis-first draft for product/ops review.
body:
Context: we have many regional COGS sheets and per-model ppk snapshots. Ops needs a compact decision surface to route live requests to cheaper equivalent variants while preserving latency SLOs and quality constraints. This doc outlines a decision-tree approach (if/then nodes) and includes example rows, sensitivity bands, and a recommended rollout plan.

Structure: the sheet mimics tree nodes as rows. Columns in the sheet: node_id, parent_id, predicate, action, expected_ppk_usd, expected_latency_ms, quality_delta_pct, confidence, notes. The idea is to compute expected_ppk_usd from the regional_unit_costs sheet and attach a conservative quality penalty.

Example node snippets (read as spreadsheet rows):
- node_id: root, parent_id: , predicate: always, action: evaluate_latency_slice, expected_ppk_usd: 0.012, expected_latency_ms: 120, quality_delta_pct: 0.0, confidence: low, notes: starting point
- node_id: latency_<100ms, parent_id: root, predicate: client_rtt < 100, action: route_preferred_low_latency_family, expected_ppk_usd: 0.028, expected_latency_ms: 60, quality_delta_pct: +0.5, confidence: high, notes: prefer fp16 V100 pool in us-west
- node_id: latency_100_400ms, parent_id: root, predicate: client_rtt >=100 && client_rtt < 400, action: route_cost_optimized_family, expected_ppk_usd: 0.0115, expected_latency_ms: 160, quality_delta_pct: -1.2, confidence: medium, notes: allow int8 quant variants
- node_id: region_emergency_fallback, parent_id: any, predicate: region_capacity_low, action: fallback_to_compatible_remote_region, expected_ppk_usd: 0.025, expected_latency_ms: 380, quality_delta_pct: -0.8, confidence: low, notes: used only when capacity < 35%

Key calculations (printed as text so the sheet can import):
- base_gpu_hour = input from regional_unit_costs (USD per GPU-hour)
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = 3_500_000 * performance_factor (example baseline for 8k seq, batch avg 1.4)
- raw_ppk = base_gpu_hour / tokens_per_gpu_hour
- kv_cache_savings = if(use_cache, 0.55, 0.0)  -- multiplier on tokens_needed
- effective_ppk = raw_ppk * (1 - kv_cache_savings) + amortized_storage_per_token + request_overhead
- amortized_storage_per_token = storage_monthly_usd / (monthly_tokens_served)
- latency_penalty_multiplier = 1 + (latency_target_ms - expected_latency_ms)/10000  (small adjustment to reflect infra premium)

Sensitivity scenarios included:
- Scenario A (conservative): spot GPU availability 60%, power cost +12%, tokens_per_gpu_hour -10% -> ppk +20%
- Scenario B (optimistic): quantization gains realized (int8) -> tokens_per_gpu_hour +40% -> ppk -28%
- Scenario C (high-cache workload): 70% prefix reuse -> kv_cache_savings 0.7 -> effective_ppk -38%

Quality guardrails: every node action must include a quality_delta_pct column. Any action that forecasts quality_loss > 2.0% must be auto-limited to < 5% of traffic in the canary stage. The sheet computes a per-candidate penalty score = expected_ppk_usd / max(0.01, (1 - quality_delta_pct/100)) to rank cost-per-quality unit.

Routing heuristics proposed:
- Prefer same-region low-latency pools for requests with rtt < 75ms, even if ppk is up to +30% more.
- For rtt between 75-250ms, apply routing to cost-optimized variants if quality_delta_pct <= 1.0 and expected_ppk_usd is at least 12% lower.
- For rtt > 250ms, aggressive cost routing allowed (ppk delta target 25% reduction) given quality_delta_pct <= 2.5 and a manual opt-out header from customers is respected.

Operational rollout plan (sheet steps):
- experiment_0: offline simulation using 30 days of token traces. Metric: estimated monthly savings vs customer-facing latency regression probability.
- experiment_1: 1% traffic canary on non-critical customers for 2 weeks. Monitor: p99 latency, error-rate, quality regression on heldout prompts.
- expand: 10% for 1 week, then 50% if no regressions.

Outputs expected from the sheet:
- per-region per-model family ppk bands (low/median/high) with confidence tags
- decision tree CSV export to be consumed by routing service
- short list of safe quantization candidates per latency slice

Appendix: example table (CSV style rows suitable for paste)
node_id,parent_id,predicate,action,expected_ppk_usd,expected_latency_ms,quality_delta_pct,confidence,notes
root,,always,evaluate_latency_slice,0.012,120,0.0,low,baseline
latency_<75ms,root,client_rtt < 75,route_low_latency_fp16,0.032,50,0.3,high,prefer us-west fp16 pool
latency_75_250ms,root,client_rtt >= 75 && client_rtt < 250,route_int8_cost,0.010,180,-1.1,medium,quantized int8 variant
region_apac_capacity_squeeze,root,region == apac && gpu_util > 0.86,route_to_nearby_region,0.023,300,0.0,low,failover to singapore-us-east crosslink

End of sheet notes. This draft intentionally mixes concrete numbers and heuristics so we can iterate quickly with SRE and models team. Please comment inline on Confluence and point to the linked simulation tickets for the tracer harness.
assumptions: tokens_per_gpu_hour baseline = 3_500_000 for A100-40GB equivalent under mixed batch
KV cache reduces active token generation by between 0.4 and 0.7 depending on workload
Spot availability varies by region; model snapshots assume 60-85% in short run

notes_to_self: Keep conservative defaults for confidence tags. Aim to have one low-risk rule that yields ~5-8% savings across global production within 8 weeks.
